questions.stem: Who was the FIRST recipient of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award — India's highest honour in cinema — conferred in 1969?

options.option_text: Devika Rani, a pioneering actress of Indian cinema
Raj Kapoor, known as the 'Showman of Bollywood'
Prithviraj Kapoor, founder of the Prithvi Theatre
V. Shantaram, pioneer of socially conscious films

questions.explanation: Devika Rani received the inaugural Dadasaheb Phalke Award in 1969 for her pioneering contributions as actress and producer in the 1930s–40s. Raj Kapoor received it in 1987; the award was not given to him first, which is the most common error.

questions.stem: The Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC), which certifies films for public exhibition in India, has its HEADQUARTERS in which city?

options.option_text: New Delhi, seat of the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Mumbai, where CBFC's main operational office is located
Chennai, home of one of India's oldest regional industries
Hyderabad, hub of the Telugu and Tamil film industries

questions.explanation: CBFC's headquarters is in Mumbai (Peddar Road), though it has regional offices across the country. Candidates often confuse this with New Delhi because the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting — under which CBFC functions — is headquartered in Delhi.

questions.stem: The Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), the country's premier institution for training in filmmaking and acting, is located in which city?

options.option_text: Mumbai, Maharashtra — close to major Bollywood studios
Hyderabad, Telangana — home of Ramoji Film City complex
Pune, Maharashtra — FTII campus established here in 1960
Kolkata, West Bengal — location of the SRFTI, not FTII

questions.explanation: FTII is located in Pune on the premises of the old Prabhat Film Company studio; it was established in 1960. The Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute (SRFTI) is its Kolkata counterpart. Confusing the two cities is the classic distractor error.

questions.stem: Which Indian film became the FIRST to win the Grand Prix (the highest award) at the Cannes Film Festival, receiving the honour at its inaugural edition in 1946?

options.option_text: Neecha Nagar (1946), directed by Chetan Anand
Pather Panchali (1955), directed by Satyajit Ray
Do Bigha Zameen (1953), directed by Bimal Roy
Awaara (1951), directed by and starring Raj Kapoor

questions.explanation: Neecha Nagar (1946) by Chetan Anand won the Grand Prix at the very first Cannes Film Festival in 1946. Pather Panchali (1955) is the more famous PYQ distractor — it won the 'Best Human Document' award at Cannes 1956, not the top prize, and came a decade later.

questions.stem: Which regional Indian film industry is popularly nicknamed 'Sandalwood'?

options.option_text: Malayalam film industry, headquartered across Kerala
Marathi film industry, mainly operating out of Pune
Odia film industry, concentrated in Bhubaneswar city
Kannada film industry, based primarily in Bengaluru

questions.explanation: The Kannada film industry is called 'Sandalwood' — a reference to Karnataka's famous sandalwood trade. Malayalam is 'Mollywood,' Marathi is 'Marollywood' or 'Marathi cinema,' and Odia is 'Ollywood.' Confusing Kannada with Malayalam is the standard distractor trap.

questions.stem: Which body is OFFICIALLY empowered to select India's annual entry for the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film?

options.option_text: Film Federation of India (FFI), an apex non-govt film body
Directorate of Film Festivals, under the Ministry of I&B
Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC), Mumbai office
National Film Development Corporation (NFDC), New Delhi

questions.explanation: The Film Federation of India (FFI) — a private apex body representing the film industry — constitutes a jury each year to select India's Oscar entry. Candidates frequently assume it is the Directorate of Film Festivals (a government body under the Ministry of I&B), which manages IFFI but does not have this Oscar-selection mandate.

questions.stem: The 1988 film 'Salaam Bombay!', which became India's first Academy Award nomination for Best Foreign Language Film in over two decades, was directed by whom?

options.option_text: Shyam Benegal, known for 'Ankur' and 'Manthan' (1976)
Mira Nair, who later directed 'Monsoon Wedding' (2001)
Govind Nihalani, known for 'Ardh Satya' and 'Tamas'
Mrinal Sen, known for 'Bhuvan Shome' and 'Akaler Sandhane'

questions.explanation: Mira Nair directed Salaam Bombay! (1988), which was shot on the streets of Mumbai with non-professional child actors. It was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film at the 61st Oscars (1989). Shyam Benegal is a strong distractor as the better-known parallel cinema director, but he did not direct this film.
